blocks.text: Understanding joins in relational algebra is crucial for efficiently querying and manipulating databases. Let's explore how different types of joins work and how they affect query results.

blocks.markdown: In relational algebra, joins are operations that allow us to combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column. Joins are fundamental to database querying and optimization.

blocks.title: Cartesian Product
blocks.text: The Cartesian product of two relations $R$ and $S$ is the set of all possible combinations of rows from $R$ and $S$. It is denoted as $R \times S$.

blocks.latex: R \times S = \{ (r, s) \mid r \in R, s \in S \}
blocks.caption: Formal definition of the Cartesian product.

blocks.markdown: While the Cartesian product is a fundamental operation, it often produces more data than needed. To refine the results, we use joins, which are essentially Cartesian products followed by selection and projection operations.

blocks.title: Theta Join
blocks.text: A theta join combines tuples from two relations based on a condition (theta). It is denoted as $R \bowtie_\theta S$.

blocks.title: Equijoin
blocks.text: An equijoin is a specific type of theta join where the condition is equality between attributes of the relations. It is a common way to combine tables.

blocks.title: Natural Join
blocks.text: A natural join is an equijoin on all attributes with the same name in the two relations, followed by the removal of duplicate columns.

blocks.title: Expressing a Natural Join
blocks.prompt: Express the natural join of relations $R(A, B)$ and $S(B, C)$ as a Cartesian product followed by selection and projection.

steps.text: 1. Perform the Cartesian product of $R$ and $S$.
2. Apply a selection to filter rows where $R.B = S.B$.
3. Project the columns $A$, $B$, and $C$ to remove duplicates.

blocks.answer: The natural join $R \bowtie S$ can be expressed as $\pi_{A, B, C}(\sigma_{R.B = S.B}(R \times S))$.

rows: Returns rows with matching values in both tables.
Returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right table.
Returns all rows from the right table and matched rows from the left table.
Returns all rows when there is a match in one of the tables.

blocks.title: Predicting Rows in a Join
blocks.prompt: Given two tables $R$ with 10 rows and $S$ with 5 rows, predict the number of rows in the result of an inner join on a common attribute.

steps.text: 1. Identify the common attribute and matching criteria.
2. Estimate the number of matching rows based on data distribution.
3. Calculate the expected number of rows in the join result.

blocks.answer: The number of rows in the inner join depends on the matching criteria. If all rows match, the result could have up to 5 rows, but it could be fewer based on actual data.

blocks.title: Join Types and Results
blocks.text: Inner joins return only matching rows, while outer joins (left, right, full) include unmatched rows from one or both tables.

points: Joins are used to combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column.
Natural joins can be expressed as a Cartesian product followed by selection and projection.
Different join types (inner, left, right, full) produce different results based on matching criteria.
